title: Rabbi Ami the Physician
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3, folio 13b: “Rabbi Yonah asked … Rabbi Ami Asya said: Rabbi Yirmeyah ruled on it.” Seder HaDorot explains that Rabbi Ami said that (Rabbi) Assi ruled, and what he ruled is what Rabbi Yirmeyah said. Hyman rejects this, arguing that Rabbi Yirmeyah was Rabbi Zeira’s student, and Rabbi Zeira too was junior to Rabbi Ami.

Hyman suggests that the reading should be “Rabbi Ami his son-in-law,” and he is Rabbi Ami (II), who was Rabbi Yonah’s son-in-law. Likewise we find in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Avodah Zarah, that Rabbi Ami asked Rabbi Yirmeyah.

notes.text: The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:3 directly reads Ami Asya reporting that Yirmeyah ruled. Hyman’s proposed “his son-in-law,” the Ami (II) identification and the chronology argument remain conjectural identifications.
